home.skills_heading: Practise every part of your inburgering
home.skills_subheading: Your inburgering has four language parts, KNM and ONA. The language parts are ready at A2 and at B1 (Listening B1 excepted), and KNM is here too: ten practice exams each, with the same structure and timing as the real exam. For ONA there is a portfolio module: eight result cards and a final interview to practise.
home.ai_subheading: Many integration practice platforms publish whatever AI generates, without anyone checking it. Some even state in their terms that they don’t guarantee it is accurate. We use AI too, but nothing goes live before our teacher has checked and corrected it.
home.social_heading: Tasks made by a certified NT2 teacher
home.social_subheading: Not random questions off the internet — every practice exam is put together and checked by a teacher who teaches integration students every week.
home.trust_1_text: Every task comes out of daily teaching practice with integration students — and out of the mistakes they make in the real exam.
home.trust_2_text: The same structure, the same number of tasks and the same timing as DUO, so nothing surprises you on exam day.
home.trust_3_text: Practise at home whenever it suits you. You see per part what you are strong at and what still needs work.
home.faq_q1: Which parts does the integration exam have?
home.faq_a1: You take four language parts: Reading, Listening, Writing and Speaking. You also take KNM (Knowledge of Dutch Society) and ONA. This platform covers the language parts at A2 and at B1, plus KNM and ONA (a portfolio module with the final interview). Only Listening B1 is still on the way.
home.faq_q2: How many tasks does each language part have?
home.faq_a2: At A2, Reading and Listening each have 25 multiple-choice questions with three options (A, B or C). Writing has 4 writing tasks and Speaking has 16 speaking tasks.
home.faq_q3: How long do the exams take?
home.faq_a3: At A2, Reading takes about 65 minutes, Listening 45, Writing 40 and Speaking 35. Our practice exams use the same timings, so you know how it feels.
home.faq_q4: How are Writing and Speaking graded?
home.faq_a4: Your answer is graded against the marking rubric our NT2 teacher wrote herself: you get a score per criterion with an explanation. The teacher reviews those gradings and adjusts the rubric where needed. So the rubric comes from a teacher, not from a model.
home.faq_a5: Practice exam 1 of every part is free and complete — not a sample, a full exam. You need no account for it. All 40 practice exams of a level need a paid subscription.
home.faq_a6: Yes, as a tool. AI helps draft tasks in DUO’s format. Our certified NT2 teacher then checks every task and corrects it where needed; only then does it go live. For Writing and Speaking a model applies her marking rubric, and she checks the gradings.

lezen.p1: In the Lezen (reading) exam you read short everyday texts: an advertisement, a letter from the gemeente, a notice at school, a leaflet or a set of rules. Each text comes with one to three multiple-choice questions. You take this exam on a computer.
lezen.p_counts: DUO's own practice exams for {level} have {items} questions in {minutes} minutes. DUO does not publish an official question count; this is what the start screen of their practice exams shows.
lezen.p3: Our ten Lezen {level} practice exams follow the same structure: the same text types, the same number of questions, the same time. After every question you see straight away whether you were right, with a short explanation from the teacher, so you learn where in the text you should have looked.
lezen.q1: How many reading practice exams does DUO have?
lezen.a1: DUO has four free Lezen A2 practice exams on inburgeren.nl. They are good for learning the format. We have ten per level, with an explanation for every question.
lezen.a2: Yes. With a free account you take practice exam 1 of every part in full, with explanations. Practice exams 2 to 10 are in the Lezen module.
lezen.q3: How many questions do I need to get right?
lezen.a3: DUO does not publish that. The pass mark is set per exam by the minister and is nowhere stated as a fixed number. Be careful with sites that quote one.

luisteren.p1: In the Luisteren (listening) exam you watch short videos and listen to conversations and announcements: at the doctor, at work, on the phone. Each fragment comes with two or three multiple-choice questions. You hear a fragment once, so you have to listen carefully the first time.
luisteren.p_counts: DUO's own practice exams for {level} have {items} questions in {minutes} minutes. DUO does not publish an official count; this is what the start screen of their practice exams shows.
luisteren.p3: Our ten Luisteren {level} practice exams are recorded by different voices at the pace of the real exam. After every question you get the teacher's explanation, and you can replay the fragment to hear what you missed.
luisteren.q1: Can I replay a fragment in the real exam?
luisteren.a1: No, in DUO's exam you hear every fragment once. Our practice exams work the same way during the exam; after you answer, you may listen again.
luisteren.a2: Yes. With a free account you take practice exam 1 in full, with explanations. Practice exams 2 to 10 are in the Luisteren module.
luisteren.a3: They help. The conversations have background noise, and headphones make the details easier to catch. In the real exam you get headphones too.

schrijven.p1: In the Schrijven (writing) exam you write short texts you really need in the Netherlands: an e-mail to a colleague, a note for the neighbours, a short piece for the neighbourhood paper, and you fill in a form. It is about being understood, not about elegant sentences.
schrijven.p_counts: DUO's own practice exams for {level} have {items} tasks, and you get {minutes} minutes.
schrijven.p_a2_only: At A2 you take this exam with pen and paper. That surprises many people who have only practised on a keyboard, so write by hand a few times during your preparation.
schrijven.p3: Our ten Schrijven {level} practice exams have the same kinds of tasks. Your answer is marked against the teacher's rubric: you see per criterion what went well and what could be better, and you compare your text with a model answer.
schrijven.a1: The teacher wrote a rubric and a model answer for every kind of task. Your feedback follows that rubric, and the teacher reviews the markings and adjusts the rubric.
schrijven.a2: Yes. With a free account you take practice exam 1 in full, with feedback. Practice exams 2 to 10 are in the Schrijven module.
schrijven.a3: Yes, but not only spelling. DUO's exam looks at whether your text is understandable, whether you wrote everything that was asked, and whether your words and sentences are correct.

spreken.p1: In the Spreken (speaking) exam you talk to the computer. You see a video or a picture, hear a question and answer out loud. You say what someone is doing, what you would do, or you explain something. Your answer is recorded.
spreken.p_counts: DUO's own practice exams for {level} have {items} questions in {minutes} minutes.
spreken.p_a2_only: At A2 there are four kinds of questions: with a video, with one picture, with two pictures you choose from, and with three pictures you use all of. You have sixty seconds per answer.
spreken.p3: Our ten Spreken {level} practice exams work exactly like that: you record your answer in the browser. Then you get feedback against the teacher's rubric and listen to a model answer, so you hear what a good answer sounds like.
spreken.q1: Do I have to speak perfect Dutch?
spreken.a1: No. At A2 what counts is that you can be understood and that you answer the question. A verb mistake does not cost you the question; no answer at all does.
spreken.a2: Yes. With a free account you take practice exam 1 in full, with feedback. Practice exams 2 to 10 are in the Spreken module.
spreken.q3: Does recording work on my phone?
spreken.a3: Yes, in the browser of your phone, tablet or computer. Nothing to install. Do practise on a laptop at least once: the real exam is taken on a computer.

level.what_title: What is the Dutch {level} inburgering exam?
level.what_p1_a2: The inburgering exam at A2 consists of four language exams: Lezen (reading), Luisteren (listening), Schrijven (writing) and Spreken (speaking). You take them separately, often on different days, and you pass them separately. On top of that you take KNM, the exam about Dutch society. At the time of writing each part costs 50 euros at DUO.
level.what_p1_b1: Under the Wet inburgering 2021, B1 is the level of the B1-route. The B1 language exam has the same four parts as A2: reading, listening, writing and speaking. The texts are longer, the tasks ask more of you, and you get more time. On top of that you take KNM.
level.what_p2: DUO publishes how long each part takes, but not the number of questions and not how many you need to get right. The numbers below come from the start screens of DUO's own practice exams. The guide on the language exams explains the format in more detail.
level.how_title: How you practise for the {level} exam here
level.how_p1: For every part there are ten practice exams with the same structure, the same number of tasks and the same time as DUO. In reading and listening you see after every question whether you were right, with an explanation. In writing and speaking you get feedback against the teacher's rubric and a model answer.
level.how_p2: Every task is drafted with the help of AI and then fully checked by a certified NT2 teacher. She decides what goes into an exam and whether it resembles what DUO asks.
level.free_p: DUO gives you three or four practice exams per part. Here you take practice exam 1 of every part for free, with an account. Want to look first without an account? Try the free ten-question practice session.
level.guide_taalexamens: The A2 and B1 language exams explained
level.b1_luisteren_note: There are no practice exams for Luisteren B1 yet. DUO publishes no practice material for it, and we do not put anything online whose format we do not know.
level.faq_title: Frequently asked questions about the {level} exam
level.q1: Can I also practise with DUO's own practice exams?
level.a1: Yes, and we recommend it. inburgeren.nl has three or four free practice exams per part. Ours have the same format; the difference is that you get ten per part and an explanation for every question.
level.q2: Do I have to take all four parts at once?
level.a2: No. You register per part with DUO and pass them independently. If you fail one part, you only retake that part.
level.q3: How many questions do I need to get right to pass?
level.a3: DUO does not publish that. The pass mark is set per exam and is nowhere stated as a fixed number. Sites that quote a number have no source for it.
level.q4: What does the inburgering exam cost?
level.a4: At the time of writing, 50 euros per part at DUO. Check the current price on inburgeren.nl. Practising here costs 9.95 euros a month per part, and practice exam 1 is free.

inburgering.meta_title: Integrating in the Netherlands: the steps explained
inburgering.meta_description: How does integrating in the Netherlands work? Which exams you take, what it costs and which law applies to you — explained simply, with every source named.
inburgering.heading: Integrating in the Netherlands, explained
inburgering.subheading: What you have to do, in what order, and where you can check it yourself. Every figure in these guides has a source.
inburgering.intro_body: Inburgering means learning Dutch and learning how the Netherlands works. You take exams at DUO. Pass them all and you get your diploma. Exactly which exams you take depends on your personal plan (PIP) and your learning route.
inburgering.phase_1_body: It states the date from which your integration period runs.
inburgering.phase_2_title: Your municipality makes a PIP with you
inburgering.phase_2_body: It sets out your learning route and which exams you take.
inburgering.phase_3_body: Usually with lessons at a language school, plus practice on your own.
inburgering.phase_4_body: Each component is a separate exam, on a separate day.
inburgering.phase_5_body: Failed one component? You retake only that one.

knm.meta_title: KNM: knowledge of Dutch society, explained
knm.meta_description: KNM is the exam component about how the Netherlands works: housing, work, healthcare, education and social customs. Here is what it is and how to prepare.
knm.heading: KNM: knowledge of Dutch society
knm.subheading: The exam component that is not about language, but about how the Netherlands works day to day.
knm.intro_body: KNM asks about living in the Netherlands: housing, work, healthcare, education, money and dealing with other people. You watch short clips and look at photos, then choose the answer that fits. It is a separate exam component, alongside the four language ones.
knm.phase_1_body: Renting, waste, noise and getting along with neighbours.
knm.phase_2_body: Applying for jobs, contracts, tax and insurance.
knm.phase_3_body: The GP, the pharmacy and how Dutch healthcare is arranged.
knm.phase_4_body: School, compulsory education and talking to your child’s teacher.
knm.phase_5_body: Making appointments, being on time and how people talk to each other.

taalexamens.intro_body: The language part of your integration consists of four exams. You take them separately, on different days. Reading and listening are multiple-choice on a computer. For writing you produce short texts yourself, and for speaking you record your answers. Each component asks something different of you, so you prepare for each one differently.
taalexamens.phase_1_body: You read short everyday texts: a letter, an email, an advert or a form. Then you answer questions about them.
taalexamens.phase_2_body: You hear conversations and short announcements, such as a phone call or a public announcement, and answer questions about what you heard.
taalexamens.phase_3_body: You fill in a form and write short texts, such as an email or a note. This component is marked by people.
taalexamens.phase_4_body: You record your answers at a computer. You respond to questions and describe what you see in a picture.

eu_citizen.title: You usually do not have to integrate
eu_citizen.body: If you come from the EU, the EEA or Switzerland, the inburgering obligation usually does not apply to you. Do you still want to learn Dutch or apply for naturalisation? Then you take the exams voluntarily.

under_18.title: You usually do not have to integrate
under_18.body: If you are under 18 and still of compulsory school age, the obligation usually does not apply. You go to school and learn Dutch there.

pension_age.title: You usually do not have to integrate
pension_age.body: If you have reached state pension age, the inburgering obligation usually does not apply to you.

temporary_stay.title: You usually do not have to integrate
temporary_stay.body: If you are in the Netherlands temporarily for work or study, the obligation usually does not apply. If you stay longer or your reason for staying changes, that can change too.

redactie.heading: How we make our content
redactie.lede: AI helps us; a teacher decides. This page explains exactly where we use AI, who checks what, and who is responsible.
redactie.resp_body: Inburgering Oefenen is run by Samen Sterk in Taal (KvK 77533216). Editorial responsibility lies with Amber van der Zalm, a certified NT2 teacher. She decides what goes online.
redactie.ai_1_body: AI drafts a first version in DUO’s format. Amber checks every exercise and corrects it. Only then does it go online.
redactie.ai_2_body: AI helps with the first draft of the Dutch text. Every figure comes from an official source, with the date we consulted it. Amber reviews the text before it goes online.
redactie.ai_3_body: These are machine-translated from the reviewed Dutch text and have not been checked by a person. Every translated page says so at the top. If in doubt, read the Dutch version.
redactie.ai_4_body: A language model applies Amber’s marking scheme to your answer. For Speaking, ElevenLabs first turns your recording into text. Amber checks the gradings. A score is practice feedback, not an official DUO result.
redactie.ai_5_body: The voices are computer-generated (ElevenLabs). The speakers are fictional characters.
redactie.ai_6_body: It works with fixed rules, not AI. It looks at your scores and tells you what to practise next.
redactie.notdo_1: No made-up reviews. The reviews on our homepage are real Trustpilot reviews of our sister site knmoefenen.nl, quoted word for word.
redactie.notdo_2: No made-up authors. Anyone shown as a teacher on this site exists and can be looked up.
redactie.notdo_3: No figures without a source. If we can’t back a number up, such as a pass mark DUO does not publish, we don’t state it.
redactie.privacy_note: Which data is used for grading is explained in our privacy policy.
redactie.errors_body: Let us know. Amber will look at it and we will fix it.
redactie.eu_note: This page also describes how we meet the transparency rules of the EU AI Act (Article 50).

ona.inl_body: DUO only checks whether everything is filled in, whether everything is about one job, and whether the evidence is included. This is how you submit your portfolio:
ona.inl_step_1: Copy your answers onto the eight official DUO result cards.
ona.inl_step_2: Make copies of your evidence: two vacancies, two application forms, your application letter and your CV.
ona.inl_step_3: Log in to Mijn Inburgering with DigiD. Choose ONA, upload the cards and the evidence, and pay €40.
ona.inl_step_4: Choose the final interview at DUO, or a 64-hour course at a school. DUO reviews your portfolio in about 6 weeks.
